sketches.title: Panic Potluck
sketches.premise: A recipe starts normally, but one cooking mistake creates the next problem. Take turns adding one thing that happens next, while the host calls the disaster like a sports announcer with no safety training.
sketches.criterion: The judge accepts one plain cooking event caused by the standing kitchen trouble, rejects a skipped cause, a finished meal or rescue, an undo of the trouble, or a newcomer the recipe and kitchen could not contain.
sketches.move_shape: Write one next event beginning with “Then,” leaving a fresh problem on the counter; example: “Then the salty soup boils over and floods the burner knobs.”
sketches.first_card: Then the onions hit the hot pan before anyone adds oil.

sketches.title: Ingredient Spiral
sketches.premise: Build one doomed dish by changing exactly one ingredient or cooking condition at a time. Every change must cause the next ugly result, and the host explains why the kitchen has now chosen violence.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that the move changes one standing recipe detail and plainly causes the next result, not a jump to a new recipe, a finished dish, a reversal, or an ingredient that appears without a possible kitchen link.
sketches.move_shape: Name one change and its immediate result in one sentence; example: “Then the extra flour makes the batter so thick that the spoon gets stuck.”
sketches.first_card: The pancake batter has one egg, two cups of flour, and no milk yet.

sketches.title: Serve at Your Own Risk
sketches.premise: A meal travels from recipe card to table, and each turn adds the next problem in its journey. The host gives savage live commentary as tiny kitchen choices create a dinner nobody can safely brag about.
sketches.criterion: The judge accepts one next event caused by the current dish or serving situation, and rejects teleporting to a new place, skipping a practical step, declaring dinner over, undoing damage, or introducing a person or object the scene cannot support.
sketches.move_shape: Start with “Then” and describe one immediate event that worsens the meal’s journey; example: “Then the loose lid pops off, splashing sauce onto the clean plates.”
sketches.first_card: The cook carries a warm pot of tomato sauce from the stove toward the table.

sketches.title: Leftovers from Hell
sketches.premise: Turn one ordinary leftover into the next questionable meal without wasting it. Each player adds one cooking step that makes the food stranger or worse, while the host hypes every cursed choice and roasts the kitchen genius behind it.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that one new food step follows from the leftover as it stands, makes a visible new problem, and does not skip preparation, end the meal, reverse a change, or summon an unrelated dish or tool.
sketches.move_shape: Add one next preparation event beginning with “Then”; example: “Then the cold noodles glue together when they hit the dry pan.”
sketches.first_card: There is a bowl of cold noodles from last night and one clean frying pan.

sketches.title: Bake Sale Breakdown
sketches.premise: Prepare one batch for a school bake sale, one mistake at a time. The host narrates like a scandal reporter, praising bold choices and blaming the player when a tiny baking error grows teeth.
sketches.criterion: The judge accepts a single next baking event caused by the current batter, oven, or sale setup, but rejects a missing link, a successful sale or cleanup, an undo, or a new scene the bake sale could not hold.
sketches.move_shape: State one immediate event with its cause and new trouble; example: “Then the cold butter leaves lumps, so the cookies bake into greasy little rocks.”
sketches.first_card: A bowl holds cookie dough, but the oven has not been turned on.

sketches.title: Midnight Snackquake
sketches.premise: Make one late-night snack while trying not to wake the house, and let each small recipe problem create the next one. The host whispers, shouts, and delivers bite-sized insults as the snack becomes a household emergency.
sketches.criterion: The judge checks that one quiet cooking or eating event follows from the standing snack trouble, while rejecting a soundless jump, a rescue or completed snack, an undo, or anything the kitchen and sleeping house could not plausibly produce.
sketches.move_shape: Begin with “Then” and add one immediate event that worsens both the snack and the risk of being heard; example: “Then the jar slips, and the metal lid smacks the tile like a tiny dinner gong.”
sketches.first_card: At midnight, someone opens the kitchen cupboard and finds a jar of peanut butter beside a loaf of bread.
